text: I'm Uday Sonawane, and this is my week on Mycroft. The checker said 725 findings. 554 of those were not defects at all. They were unbuilt work correctly described, and the number being quoted was the big one. Two episodes ago, I built the thing that counts contract mismatches between a recipe and its scripts. It reported 725 findings, and 554 of them were one message, "This step has no script." But, those were recipes marked draft, unbuilt work honestly described. A draft recipe whose scripts do not exist is not broken. It is a draft. Three questions for any count of problems. One, does this finding contradict a claim? Because

If nothing was claimed, nothing can be wrong. Two, which list did you match against? The specific one or anything that looks similar? Three, did the guard ever fire? Because a safety check that never triggers is only evidence if you know it could have. The ask was to stop counting honest states as problems, and then to fix the one that was a real problem. Question one, and the answer is a rule rather than a number. A finding is a defect when it contradicts something the recipe claims. Everything else is the honest state of unfinished work, and it gets named rather than counted. That took 725 to 171.

Then, 91 recipes got the status they were missing, and it went to 80 with 90 recipes now completely clean. Question two, and this is the one that nearly went wrong. Before stamping 91 recipes as draft, I checked whether any of them actually had working scripts, because draft would be a lie for those. The first survey came back, 42 of them do. That would have mislabeled nearly half the batch. But, that query matched any path under scripts that a recipe happened to mention, including legacy node scaffolds that exist and do nothing. Narrowed to the six canonical steps in the script locations table, the real answer is

Zero. All 91. Here is what actually got added, eight lines at the top of each file. Status draft, the count of its own open to-do's, and nulls where there is genuinely nothing yet. Question three, the generator that writes these refuses to stamp draft any recipe that does have canonical scripts on disk. It stops instead. Across all 91, that refusal never fired once. Now, a guard that never triggers is usually worth nothing as evidence. It is worth something here for one reason. The 42 survey proves it could have fired and would have if the narrow query had been wrong. Now, the part I did not plan. While checking

These numbers, I ran my own count of how many recipes carry a status line. It came back 98. The checker says 97. My command searched the whole recipes folder, so it also matched a YAML file that happens to contain the word status and is not a recipe at all. That is the same mistake as the 42 in the same week committed by the person making a video about it. Verified, the claim is that nothing below line one changed in any of the 91 files, and that is checkable from the diff alone. 91 files, 728 insertions, zero deletions, and every single hunk starting at line one and

Adding exactly eight lines. One more detail worth stealing. The open to do counts are counted per recipe, and markers that appear inside the gate test commands are excluded because two of the gates grep for to do markers, so a naive count reads too high on every recipe built from the template. Your turn. Take any list of problems your tools produce and sort it by one question. Does this contradict something we claimed, or is it just something we have not built yet? The second pile is not a backlog. It is a description. Unbuilt is not broken.
